newsitem.title: UK: Britain unmoved by asylum-seeking hunger strikers.
newsitem.headline: Britain unmoved by asylum-seeking hunger strikers.

text.p: The British government made clear on Saturday it would not intervene in a three-week hunger strike by a group of asylum seekers despite claims by their supporters that some of them could die.
Six people have been refusing to take liquids as well as food to highlight claims that their appeals for asylum in Britain are taking too long to be decided.
They are among a group of 16 people, including Russians, Somalians, Romanians and Algerians, who went on hunger strike in early January at their prison in Rochester, southern England.

"We cannot allow the situation to develop that people who do not have the right to stay in this country acquire that right by going on hunger strike," Home Secretary (interior minister) Michael Howard told BBC radio.

Doctors have said that the protesters will die if they continue to refuse liquids. Four of them, including Nigerian Pentecostalist minister Ejike Emenike, have either started drinking again or been given emergency rehydration treatment.
Howard said he hoped that the two people who were still refusing liquids would end their protest but insisted that the government would not intervene in their cases.
Campaigners against Britain's tough new rules on asylum seekers oppose the practice of holding refugees in prison while their applications to stay are processed, which can take up to two years.

Howard said, however, that only about two per cent of ayslum seekers were held in jail. He added that before the rules were changed 96 percent of people who applied for asylum in Britain were not entitled to it.
